evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle graph analysis
evidence.text: The database interprets the oracle graph as an enclosing face outline with an eye in the middle and gives ‘face’ as its original sense. It reports that 面 itself is not attested in bronze inscriptions, although a related component occurs in a bronze graph with 𦣻 and an enclosure. It identifies the enclosure as changing toward 臼 in a Chu-slip form and cites 面 ‘face toward’ in 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are the database’s analyses and citations, not direct examination of the artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 面

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 麵 is written 麪 in Shuowen, glossed 麥末也 or, in Duan Yucai’s text, 麥屑末也, and analyzed as 麥 semantic plus 丏 phonetic. It says 麵 later became a common writing and that 玉篇 and 廣韻 equate 麵 and 麪. It lists cited flour/food examples from 後漢書, 南史, and Tang poems. These citations support the recorded dictionary history but do not establish the exact date of first use or a sound borrowing from the face word.
evidence.title: A04763 麵 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.text: The 面 entry reproduces the Shuowen account: 顔前也, 从𦣻, 象人面形. It separately records face, face toward, surface and other senses with citations from classical and later texts. The citations identify sources but are not a corpus-based dating of the semantic extensions.
evidence.title: A04506 面 — 教育部《異體字字典》

Official Unihan pages failed with internal errors. Commons original file URL was established on its page but the direct fetch failed with cache miss.

search_audit.outcome: Search located and inspected the exact Commons description page for a Shuowen seal-script redraw. Page confirms modern vector provenance and public-domain release.

gaps: The available sources interpret the oracle graph as a face with an eye, but the earliest individual oracle attestations and their dates were not verified here.
The CUHK source reports no attested bronze graph for 面 itself; whether this reflects the surviving corpus or that database’s coverage remains unchecked.

The reported Chu-slip graphic change and facing sense are source assertions; the cited slip was not independently inspected. A semantic chronology for the later senses ‘surface’, ‘side’ and ‘dimension’ remains unestablished.

The Ministry dictionary supports 麪 ‘wheat flour/powder’ and the later spelling 麵, but the exact date of the graphic transition and earliest separate attestations of flour and noodle senses were not independently verified from primary texts.

No source inspected here establishes the pronunciation of the source word independently from the proposed use of 面 as 麵’s phonetic form. The Ministry entry identifies 丏, not 面, as 麪’s phonetic component; face-word history should not be treated as proof that the food word was borrowed from it.

Unihan pages for U+9762 and U+9EB5 returned internal errors. Although local rows were checked, current kMandarin readings could not be verified against accessible official upstream records in this run.

Commons oracle redraw original-image request failed with cache miss after exact URL was confirmed from its page. The seal redraw’s page and reuse terms were verified; these images are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs. No Xiaoxuetang candidate was checked.
